correctness.rationale: The real edge mass matrix is exactly (2D+W)/6; the Neumann-series comparison |(2D+W)^(-1)| <= (2D-W)^(-1) and the conservation identity C D 1 = 1 prove the bound three. Bipartite sign cancellation and nonbipartite odd closed walks make it strict for each finite graph. The cube radial recurrence and edge-shell kernel integration give the exact rational formula; resolvent distance moments S0=1/d, S1=1/(d+2), S2=(3d+2)/((d+2)(d+4)) plus the backward ratio bound establish the quantitative two-sided deficit and limit 6/d. All claims are analytically proved, with an actual 3,093-assertion exact-rational standalone checker covering finite crosschecks only.

value.rationale: Branching and independently weighted metric graphs are natural one-dimensional finite-element networks. A sharp bound uniform over all graph topologies, positive edge masses and maximum degree addresses a substantive operator-stability question. Hypercubes without degree-one vertices force the bound to be asymptotically optimal; the exact rational formula and quantified 6/d defect identify a nontrivial regular-family mechanism rather than recomputing a low-order example.
